clauses.reason: Terminated by its own terms: the employee 'is hereby exempted from the provisions of that section until December 31, 1933'. Recorded as 1933-12-31, inclusive (runs through the end of that day) under the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling; the exclusive alternative ends the exemption when that day began. Actor: EO 6168 itself.

research_rationale:
Text and identity: read in full in the registered American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-28: the page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl (a common-crawl capture, so the page can be re-fetched from the recorded WARC location) has the heading 'Executive Order 6168—Exemption of William A. Taylor from Compulsory Retirement for Age', the date 1933-06-13, which agrees with the date line of the held text, and a text_sha256 equal to the held file's. Clauses are quoted from that registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. EO 6168 (June 13, 1933, Franklin D. Roosevelt) exempts William A. Taylor, Chief, Bureau of Plant Industry, Department of Agriculture, from section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 and continues the employee in the service until December 31, 1933. Identity: number, date, person and title agree across the APP page record, the held text's date line and the census register. Legal reading: a single time-limited grant that ends by its own terms on 1933-12-31, inclusive. The searches below found no later order naming this person or citing this order, so no extension or earlier end is held. Searches made on 2026-10-28: (1) every census-register title (jobs/domesday-register/output/REGISTER.csv) containing 'retire' or 'exempt', for the person's surname and full name; (2) a full-text search of every held order text under jobs/*/output/texts (clause-drafts copies excluded) for the person's name; (3) a citation search of the same texts for this order's number in the forms 'No. N', 'Order N' and 'Orders N'. The machine USC and eCFR citation searches (complete, 0 hits) exclude a current-law reference; the OFR catalog search starts in 1937 and is not relied on alone. Authority: section 204 of Part II of the Legislative Appropriation Act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), whose proviso lets the President exempt a person from automatic separation at retirement age. No held source shows section 204 repealed or amended before this order's stated end. The held texts of EO 7945 (August 4, 1938) and EO 8231 (August 31, 1939) grant further exemptions under section 204 (cited there as 5 U.S.C. 715a), which corroborates that the statutory scheme was still in force through the stated end of every exemption submitted in this batch (the latest is January 1, 1938).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own-terms end on the stated 'until' date. Under the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling the end is recorded as that date, inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, under which the exemption stops when that day begins, is the stated alternative. The employee's death or separation before the date would leave the exemption unused but is not, on the order's text, an end of the order, and no held record shows such an event. The date is a fixed term of the grant, not a deadline on some other act. No held order revokes, amends or shortens this exemption.","independent_command_check":"The order contains one operative command, the time-limited exemption of one named employee.
